source.title: Steam condenser: independent calculation with CoolProp (IAPWS-95), no published case
source.licence: CoolProp is MIT licensed; the values are computed here
source.fetch_route: not a document: values computed 2026-11-20 with CoolProp PropsSI('H', 'T', ..., 'P', ..., 'Water') at 101.325 kPa
source.note: a cooler case with a phase change, which the DWSIM tutorial's liquid-only cooler does not cover; the source of truth is the water property formulation, not another simulator

basis.enthalpy_reference: each simulator's own; the duty is the stream enthalpy difference times the mass flow, so the reference does not depend on it

P.anchor: specified for this case: no pressure drop

reported.name: condenser_duty
reported.anchor: CoolProp IAPWS-95: h(60 C liquid) - h(120 C vapour) at 101.325 kPa, 1 kg/s (-2465.251 kW)

reported.name: cond_vapor_fraction
reported.anchor: 60 C is far below the saturation temperature of 99.97 C at 1 atm: all liquid

tolerance.note: the duty is dominated by the latent heat of condensation (about 2257 kJ/kg), which each package predicts differently

scenarios.why: cool to 99 C, just below the saturation temperature: still full condensation, duty -2301.549 kW
cool only to 105 C: sensible heat of the vapour, no condensation, duty -30.572 kW (a small number difference of two enthalpies, so relative errors look larger)

review.method: duties recomputed independently with CoolProp (IAPWS-95); the outlet specification is read back
